title: Why You Always Feel The Need To Return A Favour
hook: You just got a free coffee. Now you feel obligated.

narration.text: When someone gives you something, even small, you feel a strong urge to reciprocate.
This isn't just politeness; it is a fundamental social rule.
Our brains are wired to balance the scales of giving and taking.
Breaking this rule can lead to social discomfort or even exclusion.
It builds trust and cooperation, essential for human societies.
Notice this feeling next time someone holds a door for you.
Tell us in the comments what small favour you felt compelled to return, like this if it surprised you, and subscribe for more insights into your mind.

description: Ever wondered why you feel compelled to return a favour, even a tiny one? It's a powerful psychological principle called reciprocity, deeply ingrained in our social behaviour. This short explains the underlying mechanism and why it's so crucial for human interaction.
topic: Why you often feel a powerful urge to return a favour, even a small one. This is a common social rule of reciprocity.
